events.title: Certiorari Granted in Martin v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari in the case of Martin, Curtrina, et al. v. United States, et al., docket number 24-362. The Court will review two specific legal questions: whether the Constitution’s Supremacy Clause bars claims under the Federal Tort Claims Act when federal employees' actions further federal policy, and whether the discretionary-function exception is inapplicable to claims under the law enforcement proviso to the intentional torts exception. The petitioners' brief is due by March 7, 2025, the respondents' brief by April 1, 2025, and the reply brief by April 22, 2025.
events.why_relevant: The case addresses significant questions about the scope of federal liability and the application of constitutional principles to federal tort claims.

events.title: Disbarment Orders Issued for Multiple Attorneys
events.summary: The Supreme Court issued orders disbarring several attorneys from the practice of law in the Court. These attorneys, including Christopher Craig Humphrey, Maureen Callahan Repetto, Michael Todd Hogan, Edward Paul Brueggeman, Dorothea Jane Kingsbury, Thomas Patrick Connelly, Jr., Dennis Lee Adams, and Andrew Douglas Purcell, had previously been suspended and failed to respond to show cause orders.
events.why_relevant: Disbarment orders maintain the integrity of the legal profession and ensure that attorneys practicing before the Court adhere to ethical standards.

events.title: Fields v. Colorado: Certiorari Granted and Case Remanded
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of petitioner Troy Fields for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and the petition for a writ of certiorari. The judgment was vacated, and the case was remanded to the Court of Appeals of Colorado for further consideration in light of the precedent set by Erlinger v. United States, 602 U.S. 821 (2024). This decision indicates that the lower court's ruling may not have fully considered the implications of the Erlinger case.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's decision to vacate and remand the case underscores the importance of consistent application of legal precedents.

events.title: Riley v. McHenry: Motion to Seal Granted
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of petitioner Pierre Y. N. Riley to seal the appendix to the petition for a writ of certiorari and for leave to file the joint appendix under seal, with redacted copies for the public record. This procedural decision allows certain sensitive information to remain confidential while still providing a public record.
events.why_relevant: This order highlights the balance between transparency and privacy in judicial proceedings.

events.title: Invitation for Amicus Curiae in Martin v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court has invited Christopher Mills, Esquire, of Charleston, South Carolina, to brief and argue the case of Martin v. United States, et al., as amicus curiae. This invitation is specifically in support of the judgment below concerning the first question identified in the order granting the petition for a writ of certiorari.
events.why_relevant: The Court's invitation for an amicus curiae highlights the importance of the legal questions involved, which may influence future legal interpretations.

events.title: Invitation for Amicus Curiae in Parrish v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court has invited Michael R. Huston, Esquire, of Washington, D.C., to brief and argue the case of Parrish v. United States as amicus curiae. This invitation is in support of the judgment below, indicating the Court's interest in additional perspectives on the case. The involvement of an amicus curiae suggests the case may have broader implications or complexities that require further examination.
events.why_relevant: The invitation for an amicus curiae indicates the Court's interest in a thorough examination of the case, potentially affecting the interpretation of law.

events.title: Certiorari Denied in Bowman v. Stirling
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the application for a stay of execution of Marion Bowman, as well as the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case Bowman v. Stirling, Director, South Carolina Department of Corrections, et al. This decision means that the execution of the death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of death penalty cases.
